answer: One defence is a bonded-identity river: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit sits on a public ledger like quartz in clear rock — visible, verifiable, and costly to duplicate. New identities start on a small island of trust with tiny limits, earning larger limits only through months of honest trades, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits and a thousand slow reputations, while one honest agent pays once.
